description: Set WARMDOWN_RATIO to 0.3 so more training time is spent at peak learning rate.
Set DEPTH to 6 so a smaller, faster model sees more tokens in the 300 s budget.
Set HEAD_DIM to 64 so the model uses 12 attention heads at dim 512 (n_kv_head follows num_heads automatically).
Add a learnable per-layer scalar (init 1.2) multiplying q after QK RMS norm to sharpen attention logits, optimized with Adam.
Double the unembedding (lm_head) Adam learning rate from 0.004 to 0.008.
Replace the MLP's relu-squared with SwiGLU (hidden dim 8/3*n_embd rounded up to a multiple of 64) at a similar parameter count.
No change: train.py already applies the logit softcap with softcap = 15 (the spec assumed 30).
No change: train.py already decays Muon weight decay linearly to zero via get_weight_decay(progress) = WEIGHT_DECAY * (1 - progress), applied each step to the muon param groups.
Clip the global gradient norm to 1.0 after the backward passes and before the optimizer step.
Raise EMBEDDING_LR from 0.6 to 0.9 and set FINAL_LR_FRAC to 0.05 so the LR does not decay fully to zero.
Halve TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE to 2**18 (grad accumulation 4 -> 2) and set WARMDOWN_RATIO to 0.3, leaving all LRs unchanged.
Set WARMUP_RATIO to 0.02 so the learning rate ramps up over the first 2% of the time budget.
Clip the global gradient norm to 1.0 after all micro-batch backward passes and before optimizer.step().
Raise MATRIX_LR from 0.04 to 0.06 and end the Muon momentum ramp at 0.97 instead of 0.95.
Residual projections are already zero-initialized, so only halve the token embedding init std from 1.0 to 0.5.

issues: The diff contains only the comment line '# candidate edit withheld'. The real change to train.py is not shown, so I could not check it for tampering with val_bpb measurement, data, seed lines or the evaluation call (item 1), or for bugs (item 2).
If the diff is complete, the candidate is functionally the same as the incumbent, and the 0.0025 difference (1.0973 vs 1.0998) is run-to-run noise.

I can't recompute z: with one candidate run and one incumbent run there is no spread to compute it from. The reported z=0.344 implies a spread of about 0.0073, which must come from an outside estimate I can't verify.
The provisional reject matches the numbers: the improvement is not statistically meaningful at z=0.344.
No veto, because the visible diff shows no tampering or bug. The full diff should be provided and re-reviewed before any acceptance.

description: Set ADAM_BETAS to (0.9, 0.99) and WARMUP_RATIO to 0.02 for smoother Adam moments and a brief LR warmup.
No change: train.py already has TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE = 2**18 with DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 64, so grad accumulation is already 2.
Set SCALAR_LR to 0.25 and UNEMBEDDING_LR to 0.008 on top of the incumbent.

issues: Integrity: no problem. The diff changes only two hyperparameters: UNEMBEDDING_LR goes from 0.004 to 0.008 and SCALAR_LR from 0.5 to 0.25. It does not touch the seed lines, the prepare.py import, the data, the evaluation call or the summary printing. I found no bug that would make the result meaningless.

I could not reproduce z = 1.522 from the numbers given. The candidate mean is 1.0900, which is 0.0098 lower (better) than the incumbent's 1.0998. The sample SD of the two candidate runs is about 0.00339. A two-sample z using that SD is 0.0098 / (0.00339 * sqrt(1/2 + 1/1)) ≈ 2.36. The harness figure implies a standard error of about 0.00644, so it probably uses a fixed or pooled noise SD that isn't shown. Either way the sign and the accept decision agree.

The evidence is thin. The incumbent has only one run, and an SD estimated from two candidate runs is unreliable. The gain could still be noise near the borderline, so another incumbent run would make the decision firmer.
The two learning rates were changed together, so this result can't say which change helped.

description: Set SCALAR_LR to 0.25 and UNEMBEDDING_LR to 0.008 on top of the incumbent.
Set DEPTH to 10 and ASPECT_RATIO to 48 (dim 480 rounds up to 512), giving a deeper model at the same width.
Set WARMDOWN_RATIO to 0.6 and make the warmdown decay follow a cosine curve instead of linear.
Halve TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE to 2**17 (grad accumulation 2 -> 1) to get more optimizer steps in the 300 s budget.
Set weight_decay to 0.01 on the token-embedding and value-embedding Adam groups, using the existing decoupled decay in adamw_step_fused.
